fontGenerator.title: Tattoo Font Generator: Preview Your Name in 18 Tattoo Fonts
fontGenerator.description: Type a name, date or quote and preview it in 18 tattoo fonts: script, Old English, gothic, blackletter, typewriter and more. Free, instant, no sign-up. Then try it on your skin with TattooLab.
fontGenerator.intro: Type a name, a date or a short quote and see it in 18 classic tattoo lettering styles. Pick the one that fits, then try it on your skin, live, with the TattooLab app before you book.
tips: Script fonts look elegant small, but leave space between letters: lines that sit too close blur together as a tattoo ages.
Old English and blackletter read best at 4 cm tall or more.
Typewriter and clean serif fonts suit dates, coordinates and short quotes.
Print your favourite at 100% and bring it to your artist: they will adjust the letterforms to your skin and placement.

ideasHub.title: Tattoo Ideas: Small, Fine Line, Matching, Cover-Up and Flash
ideasHub.description: Hand-picked tattoo ideas with placement tips and how each style ages. Browse small, fine line, matching, cover-up and Friday the 13th flash ideas, then try any design on your skin with TattooLab.
ideasHub.intro: Ideas grouped the way people actually plan a tattoo: by size, style and moment. Every idea comes with a placement tip and a note on how it ages, so the design you love today still looks good in 20 years.

ideas.title: Small Tattoo Ideas That Age Well (With Placement Tips)
ideas.description: Small tattoo ideas for wrists, ankles, fingers and behind the ear, with honest notes on how tiny tattoos age. Try any idea on your skin before you ink with TattooLab.
ideas.intro: Small tattoos are the most popular first tattoo, and the most likely to blur. The trick is a simple silhouette, enough space inside the lines and a placement that doesn't rub all day.

items.name: Single-stem rose
items.text: A long stem with two leaves keeps the design open. Inner forearm or ankle, about 6–8 cm.

items.name: Crescent moon and star
items.text: Two shapes, almost no detail: one of the few designs that still reads clearly at 2 cm. Behind the ear or wrist.

items.name: Olive branch
items.text: A slight curve follows the bone of the wrist or collarbone. Keep at least 1 mm between leaves.

items.name: Tiny butterfly
items.text: Choose bold outer wings and skip fine inner patterns; they fill in over the years.

items.name: Paper plane
items.text: Clean triangles and a dotted trail. Works on the side of a finger, though finger tattoos fade faster.

items.name: Initials in typewriter font
items.text: Two letters, 1–1.5 cm tall, on the inner wrist. Try fonts with the Tattoo Font Generator first.

ideas.aging: Very small, detailed tattoos are the first to blur. If you love a design, go up one size: 8 cm instead of 5 keeps lines readable for decades. TattooLab's Aging Simulator shows how your exact design may look after 10, 20 and 30 years.

ideas.title: Fine Line Tattoo Ideas: Delicate Designs and How They Age
ideas.description: Fine line tattoo ideas: botanicals, single-line portraits, constellations and script. Learn which fine line designs hold up over time and preview them on your skin with TattooLab.
ideas.intro: Fine line tattoos use a single thin needle for delicate, sketch-like work. They are beautiful and quick to heal, but they need the right design and placement to stay crisp.

items.name: Botanical sprig
items.text: Lavender, olive or eucalyptus along the forearm. The natural spacing between leaves is ideal for fine line.

items.name: Single-line face
items.text: One continuous line drawing a profile. Keep it at least 7 cm tall so the line stays clean.

items.name: Constellation
items.text: Dots and thin connecting lines on the shoulder blade or ribs. Ask for slightly larger dots so they don't fade.

items.name: Script word
items.text: A word in a light script along the collarbone. Preview the letter spacing in the Tattoo Font Generator.

items.name: Geometric compass
items.text: Fine lines with a few bolder accents give depth without crowding.

items.name: Wave line
items.text: A minimalist ocean wave on the ankle or wrist.

ideas.aging: Fine line work softens faster than bold outlines, especially on hands, feet and areas in the sun. Choose designs with breathing room and protect them with sunscreen; TattooLab's Tattoo Care has a day-by-day healing guide.

ideas.title: Matching Tattoo Ideas for Couples, Friends and Siblings
ideas.description: Matching tattoo ideas for couples, best friends and siblings: sun and moon, lock and key, coordinates and more. Try both designs on live before you commit with TattooLab.
ideas.intro: The best matching tattoos are two halves of one idea: each looks complete on its own and tells the full story together. Pick something that will still feel right years from now.

items.name: Sun and moon
items.text: One sun, one moon, same line weight. Inner wrists, so they meet when you hold hands.

items.name: Lock and key
items.text: A classic for couples. Keep both pieces the same size and style.

items.name: Two paper planes
items.text: Great for long-distance friendships: same plane, flying in opposite directions.

items.name: Coordinates
items.text: The place you met, in a typewriter font. Simple, personal and readable.

items.name: Two halves of a heart
items.text: A single-line heart split down the middle, one half each.

items.name: Siblings' birth flowers
items.text: Each person gets their own birth flower in the same style, so the set grows with the family.

ideas.aging: Matching tattoos rarely age the same way: placement, skin and sun exposure all differ. Make them a little larger than you think and use the same artist so the line weight matches. Try both on live with TattooLab to check size and placement first.

ideas.title: Friday the 13th Tattoo Flash Ideas (Lucky 13 Designs)
ideas.description: Friday the 13th flash day ideas: black cats, horseshoes, lucky 13, daggers and clovers. Design your own lucky flash and try it on your skin before you go with TattooLab.
ideas.intro: On Friday the 13th, tattoo shops celebrate with flash day: small, ready-to-go designs, often around $13 plus tip. Lines get long, so it pays to know what you want before you go.

items.name: Lucky number 13
items.text: Bold old-school numerals with a banner or stars. The most classic flash day pick.

items.name: Black cat
items.text: Arched back, yellow eyes, sometimes sitting in a horseshoe. Bad luck turned into a lucky charm.

items.name: Horseshoe
items.text: Open end up to hold the luck in. Pairs well with a 13 or a few stars.

items.name: Clover and dagger
items.text: A four-leaf clover pierced by a small dagger: luck with an edge.

items.name: Dice
items.text: A pair of dice showing six and seven. Small, bold and easy to place.

items.name: Crescent moon with a face
items.text: Traditional moon in bold outline and yellow fill.

ideas.aging: Traditional flash ages beautifully: bold outlines and solid fills stay readable for decades. In TattooLab's Design Studio, the Friday the 13th Flash pack (Nov 7–13) gives you these ideas in one tap, and Try On Live shows it on your arm in real time.

ideas.title: Cover-Up Tattoo Ideas: Turn an Old Tattoo Into New Art
ideas.description: Cover-up tattoo ideas that work: florals, animals, mandalas and blackwork. Learn how cover-ups are planned, how many sessions they take, and preview ideas over your old tattoo with TattooLab.
ideas.intro: A good cover-up doesn't hide the old tattoo, it uses it. Dark, textured designs absorb old lines, and the new piece is usually about two to three times the size of the original.

items.name: Peonies and roses
items.text: Layered petals and dark shading hide old script and small symbols well.

items.name: Animal portrait
items.text: A wolf, lion or tiger with dense fur texture covers tribal and faded black work.

items.name: Mandala
items.text: Symmetric and dense; great over round or centered old tattoos.

items.name: Dragon or koi
items.text: Japanese styles with waves and scales can cover a large area in one flowing design.

items.name: Blackwork band
items.text: For very dark old tattoos, a solid geometric band is often the cleanest answer.

items.name: Feathers and wings
items.text: Directional texture follows the old lines and breaks up their shape.

ideas.aging: Cover-ups often need two to four sessions, and very dark old ink may need a few laser sessions to lighten it first. TattooLab's Cover-Up Advisor analyses a photo of your old tattoo, suggests ideas with difficulty and sessions, and lets you compare before and after.

guidesHub.title: Tattoo Guides: Pain Chart, Aftercare, Aging and Try-On
guidesHub.description: Practical tattoo guides before and after you ink: pain chart by body part, day-by-day aftercare, how tattoos age, AI tattoo design and virtual try-on.
guidesHub.intro: Everything worth knowing before and after you get tattooed, written to help you plan a tattoo you'll still love in 30 years.

guides.title: AI Tattoo Generator: Turn Your Idea Into a Tattoo Design
guides.description: Describe your idea and get original tattoo designs in seconds: fine line, blackwork, traditional, realism, Japanese and more. Try the design on your skin and print a stencil for your artist with TattooLab.
guides.intro: An AI tattoo generator turns a short description, or a reference photo, into a tattoo-ready design. Used well, it is the fastest way to explore ideas before you sit down with your artist.

p: Write what you want in a sentence: the subject, the mood and where it will go. For example: "Icarus falling toward the sun, black and grey realism, inner forearm". Pick a style, the ink (black and grey or color) and the size, and TattooLab's Design Studio creates an original design on clean paper.
You can add a photo of a pet, a place or an old sketch, and the generator keeps its recognizable shape while turning it into tattoo linework.

list: Name one main subject; crowded prompts make crowded tattoos.
Say the style out loud: fine line, blackwork, American traditional, neo-traditional, irezumi, realism or geometric.
Mention the placement and size so the composition fits the body part.
Generate a few versions, then combine the best parts with your artist.

p: A design that looks great on paper still has to work on a curved, moving arm. Use Try On Live to see it on your body through the camera, the Aging Simulator to check it in 10 to 30 years, then print a 100% stencil and bring it to your artist.

faq: Can I take an AI tattoo design to my tattoo artist?
Yes. Most artists welcome a clear reference. They will redraw it for your skin and placement, which is exactly what you want.
Are AI tattoo designs original?
TattooLab generates a new image for every request. Don't ask for copies of other artists' work; describe your own idea instead.
Is it free?
TattooLab includes free AI generations to try it, then a Pro subscription for more.

guides.title: Virtual Tattoo Try-On: See a Tattoo on Your Body Before You Ink
guides.description: Try any tattoo design on your arm, leg, chest or back live through your iPhone camera. Free, on-device virtual tattoo try-on with TattooLab: check size, placement and style before you book.
guides.intro: A tattoo is permanent; trying it on shouldn't be. Virtual try-on puts the design on your own skin in real time so you can check size, angle and placement before the first line.

p: Open a design in TattooLab and tap Try On Live. Point the rear camera at your forearm, upper arm, chest, back or leg. The design's paper background disappears and the ink is blended into your skin so its texture shows through. Apple's body-pose detection keeps it anchored to the body part as you move.
Drag, pinch and rotate to adjust, set the ink strength, then take a photo to share with friends or your artist. It runs entirely on your iPhone and doesn't use AI credits.

sections.h: What to check while trying it on
list: Size: can you read every detail from a normal distance?
Flow: does the design follow the muscle and bone instead of fighting them?
Visibility: is it where you want it to be seen, or hidden at work?
Movement: twist your arm; good placements still look right in motion.

faq: Do I need to buy anything to try on tattoos?
No. Try On Live is free and runs on your iPhone.
Which body parts work best?
Forearms, upper arms, calves and the back work best because the camera can see the whole body part. Very small areas like fingers are better checked on a photo.
Is the try-on realistic?
It blends the ink into your skin and follows your movement, but it is a preview: a real tattoo depends on your artist, skin and healing.

guides.title: Tattoo Aging: What Will My Tattoo Look Like in 10, 20, 30 Years?
guides.description: How tattoos age and why: line spread, fading, sun and placement. See your own design after 5, 10, 20 and 30 years with TattooLab's tattoo aging simulator.
guides.intro: Every tattoo changes. Ink particles slowly spread under the skin, lines soften and colors fade, faster in the sun and on areas that move or rub a lot. Planning for that is the difference between a tattoo that holds up and one that blurs.

list: Line spread: thin lines widen a little every year, so tiny details merge.
Fading: color and grey wash lighten, especially with sun exposure.
Skin changes: elasticity and texture change with age and weight.
Placement: hands, feet, fingers and lips fade fastest; the outer arm, calf and back hold up best.

p: Bold outlines, open space between lines, strong contrast and a size that matches the detail. If a design has many small elements, go a size up. Black and grey usually outlasts pastel colors.

TattooLab's Aging Simulator takes your design or a photo of your tattoo and shows how it may look after 5, 10, 20 and 30 years based on placement, skin type, sun exposure, style and ink. Results are estimates, but they make the trade-offs easy to see before you commit.

faq: Do fine line tattoos fade faster?
They tend to soften sooner because the lines are thin. Bigger designs with more spacing hold up better.
How can I slow down tattoo aging?
Sunscreen on healed tattoos, moisturized skin, and a good artist who sets the ink at the right depth.
Can an old tattoo be refreshed?
Yes. Many artists can re-line or add contrast, or plan a cover-up.

guides.title: Tattoo Pain Chart: Least and Most Painful Places to Get Tattooed
guides.description: Tattoo pain chart by body part: the least painful places (outer arm, forearm, thigh, calf) and the most painful (ribs, spine, feet, hands). Tips to make your session easier.
guides.intro: Pain is personal, but most people feel it the same way: areas with more muscle and fat hurt less, and areas over bone, nerves or thin skin hurt more. Use this chart to pick a placement for your first tattoo or plan a big session.

head: Body part
Pain (1–10)
Why
rows: Thick skin and muscle, few nerve endings
Muscle padding; the most common first tattoo
Muscle, but tender near the shin
Depends on muscle; sternum is high
Thin skin over bone and nerves
Thin skin over bone, moves with breathing
Armpit, elbow ditch, back of knee

list: Eat a proper meal and drink water before the session.
Sleep well and skip alcohol the night before.
Ask for short breaks on long sessions.
Start with a lower-pain placement for your first tattoo.

sections.h: Check the pain before you choose
p: TattooLab's InkMaster reviews your design and shows a pain map for different placements, so you can pick a spot you'll actually sit through. Then use Try On Live to see the design there.

faq: Where is the least painful place to get a tattoo?
The outer upper arm, outer forearm and outer thigh are usually the least painful.
Where does a tattoo hurt the most?
Ribs, spine, armpits, the elbow ditch, the back of the knee, hands and feet.
Does tattoo pain get worse over a long session?
Often yes: skin becomes sensitive after a few hours. Splitting a big piece into sessions helps.

guides.title: Tattoo Aftercare Day by Day: Healing Timeline and Tips
guides.description: A day-by-day tattoo aftercare guide: the first 48 hours, peeling and itching in week 1–2, and long-term care. What's normal, what isn't, and how to keep your tattoo sharp.
guides.intro: A new tattoo is a healing wound. Most heal on the surface in two to four weeks and fully in about two to three months. Good aftercare keeps it clean, comfortable and sharp. Always follow your artist's instructions first.

head: When
What happens
What to do
rows: Oozing of plasma and ink, redness, tenderness
Keep the wrap on as long as your artist says, then wash gently with lukewarm water and unscented soap, pat dry
Thin layer of unscented moisturizer 2–3 times a day; no soaking
Don't scratch or pick; let flakes fall off on their own

list: Swimming pools, the sea, baths and saunas
Direct sun and tanning
Tight clothes rubbing the area
Scratching or picking scabs

p: Some redness and swelling is normal in the first days. Redness that spreads or grows after day 3, increasing pain, heat, pus, red streaks or a fever can mean infection: see a doctor promptly.
TattooLab's Tattoo Care lets you scan your healing tattoo and follow a day-by-day journey with reminders. It is general guidance, not medical advice.

faq: How long does a tattoo take to heal?
The surface usually heals in 2–4 weeks; deeper layers take about 2–3 months.
When can I swim after a tattoo?
Wait until it's fully healed on the surface, usually 2–4 weeks, and follow your artist's advice.
Is it normal for a new tattoo to peel?
Yes. Peeling and itching in the first two weeks are normal; don't pick at it.
